notes.meaning: The prophet asks who has truly believed the good news about God's Servant. God showed his mighty saving power through the Messiah, but very few people recognized it. Most people expected worldly greatness and failed to see God working in someone humble.

The Servant grew up quietly under God's watchful care, like a small green shoot in dry ground. He came from a family line that had lost its royal standing, living in ordinary, poor conditions. He had no outward glamour or worldly majesty to make people run after him.

People looked down on the Servant and turned away from him in disgust. He spent his life facing hardship and was deeply familiar with sorrow and suffering. Instead of honoring him, people treated him as though he had no value at all.

The Servant carried the heavy pains and sicknesses that belong to our fallen world. The people watching him thought God was striking him down for his own wrongdoing. In truth, he was taking our burdens and suffering in our place.

The Servant was pierced and crushed to pay for our sins and rebellions against God. The punishment he took brought us peace, meaning he restored our friendship with God. Through the wounds he suffered on his body, our souls are healed.

differ.view: Believers receive bodily healing from sickness as a blessing provided in Christ's death on the cross, though total physical healing will be completed when he returns.
Christ provided for bodily healing in his sacrifice, but believers debate when that healing is meant to take place.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Some teachers claim this verse promises every believer complete physical health right now, so that staying sick means a person lacks faith.

notes.meaning: All human beings have wandered away from God like lost, stubborn sheep. Each person chose to follow their own selfish path instead of obeying him. Yet the Lord gathered up the guilt and punishment of everyone and placed it directly onto his Servant.

The Servant was mistreated and abused, but he never complained or spoke an angry word in defense. He went willingly to his death like a gentle lamb led to slaughter, or a quiet sheep being sheared. He stayed completely in control and quietly obeyed God's plan to save others.

An unfair legal trial and violent treatment took the Servant away to be killed. The people of his day never stopped to realize that he was dying for their sins rather than his own. He was cut off from life so he could take the blow that God's people deserved.

Men planned for him to be buried among criminals, but he was placed in the tomb of a rich man after he died. He never harmed anyone or told a single lie during his life. God arranged an honorable burial for him because he was entirely innocent and pure.

The Lord permitted his Servant to suffer and die as a guilt offering, which is a sacrifice made to make amends for wrongdoing. Because he willingly gave up his life, he will rise from the dead and see a vast spiritual family of believers. God's wonderful plan of salvation will completely succeed in his hands.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: God did not punish his Son with divine wrath, but permitted him to offer a loving sacrifice that pays humanity's debt.

notes.meaning: After enduring such terrible suffering, the Servant will look on the results of his work with deep joy. By knowing him and trusting in his sacrifice, many people will be justified, meaning God forgives them and counts them righteous. He accomplishes this by taking the weight of their sins upon himself.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Bearing sins describes an atoning sacrifice made on our behalf, not Christ taking on personal guilt or being condemned in our place.

notes.meaning: God rewards the Servant with the high honor of a mighty ruler dividing the spoils of victory. He receives this reward because he poured out his life unto death and allowed himself to be counted among criminals. Even while dying, he carried the sins of many and prayed for the very people who wronged him.
